name: infra_registry_plugins
title: A decorator Registry (detectron2 / mmdet / timm / fairseq idiom): the model, the loss and the optimizer are strings in a dict
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-infra: the plugin-registry project shape
note: A pure precision trap on a workspace whose three central objects are only reachable through `@REGISTRY.register("name")` decorators and a `dict[name]` lookup. MLView reports nothing - correct - and declares two `unresolved_callee` gaps naming the exact two calls it could not read (registry.Registry.build line 43 and OPTIMIZERS.get line 72) plus an `untagged_dataflow` gap saying the backward at line 89 carries a value it could not type. That is the honest answer to a registry. Two reporting observations, neither a finding and neither labelled: the objective card names `bce (torch.nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits) at plugins.py:67`, which is an internal term inside FocalLoss.forward rather than the criterion the loop optimises, and it names BOTH registered optimizer factories (AdamW at plugins.py:76 and SGD at plugins.py:81) although CONFIG["optimizer"]["name"] is the literal "adamw" in a module-level dict MLView does resolve. See the domain-infra round-2 report, finding INFRA-R2-15.
stagesObserved: config, data, model, objective, train, eval and deliver present; preprocess absent, which is correct.

forbidden.why: the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 54
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False at line 56
no DataLoader here passes num_workers, and the module ends in `if __name__ == "__main__": main()`
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is at line 86, before the forward at 87
optimizer.step() is called at line 91, after loss.backward() at line 89
the order is zero_grad (86) -> forward (87) -> loss (88) -> backward (89) -> clip (90) -> step (91)
the epoch loss is accumulated as running += loss.item(), a Python float
FocalLoss.forward builds its terms and returns (weight * bce).mean(); there is no accumulator outside a loop and no loop at all in that method
CosineAnnealingLR is epoch-cadence and scheduler.step() is called at line 93, in the epoch loop after the batch loop closes
clip_grad_norm_ at line 90 sits between the backward at 89 and the step at 91
model.eval() is called at line 95 before the validation block and model.train() at line 106 on the way out
the validation block is wrapped in `with torch.no_grad():` at line 98
the accuracy comparison at line 102 is on model(features).argmax(dim=1), not on raw logits
neither registered model applies a softmax; both return self.head(...) and the registered cross_entropy factory is fed exactly that
FocalLoss takes logits and calls F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits itself at line 67; there is no sigmoid anywhere in this workspace, which is what the with-logits form requires
the model is moved at line 68 and both loops move every batch value to the same device before the forward (84-85 and 100-101)
the device is chosen behind torch.cuda.is_available() at line 65

seed_everything(CONFIG["seed"]) at line 63 calls random.seed, numpy.random.seed, torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed_all, and the training loader passes generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(CONFIG["seed"])
there is no sklearn splitter and no random_split; the cut is the literal index 6400 and the loader carries an explicit generator
WideResNet.__init__, TinyMLP.__init__ and FocalLoss.__init__ all call super().__init__() as their first statement
the residual blocks are built inside nn.ModuleList(...) at line 23; there is no plain list or dict of submodules
torch.save stores model.state_dict() at line 112 and nothing in this workspace calls torch.load

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV903 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: `import plugins` at train.py:26 is what performs the registration; the registered classes are reached from the entrypoint through MODELS.build / LOSSES.build and are not orphans
